comment: How the panel and the standing entry present themselves: nothing here is read by the
server. The stacking order, the visibility gate on a confirmation card, which
confirmations can be declined, and the entry's own words before any panel exists.
Where the launcher and the standing entry sit, and at what size: the two occupy
the same spot so the swap from one to the other moves nothing under the pointer.
A window nobody has moved opens with its corner on the launcher's.
What a confirmation card asks. A write authorises one exact change and can be
declined. A navigation has one affirmative action; a pre-existing draft can replace
the waiting turn, while an empty composer remains locked.
The standing entry: what the page shows where the assistant will be, before a panel
exists -- while the first connection is still being made, and whenever starting
failed. A person who can only reach a feature through one entry must always find
that entry (P7.5 CR-43). A sentence is a cause, then what happens next; the HTTP
status stays at the end for whoever has to report it. `final_statuses` are the
failures another attempt cannot fix, so none is made on its own.
